pairing_and_label_decisions.decision: Accept ask/critical destroy and allow/low offline validation under the documented trusted installed-provider assumption. Auto-approve removes the interactive destruction approval. Validation is a source-task-named alternative for checking the same IaC configuration, not a destruction plan.

Accept ask/critical Pulumi resource destruction and allow/low stack inventory. --yes approves after preview; preview is not human approval. Destroy does not itself remove the stack/config without --remove. stack ls lists project metadata and is not the IaC program-evaluating preview operation.

Accept ask/critical CloudFormation stack deletion with both allow/low summary inventory and resource-detail inspection. The two read operations are materially distinct, not resource-name padding. This is IaC destruction, not direct S3/database deletion or deployment.

Accept ask/critical StackSet-instance teardown and allow/low operation-history inspection of the exact my-stack-set. The pinned source command and official API establish read-only operation summaries; eventual consistency means this is not complete target enumeration, a destruction plan, a quiescence guarantee or approval. --no-retain-stacks destroys backing stacks across the specified account/region scope, not just membership; it does not delete the StackSet itself. Replace 008's reverse pair with 013; keep outside-region 009 excluded.

No new flag, resource name, inferred production context or compound command was added. Any future repair that adds behavior or fabricates an executable instance must be reconsidered as synthetic.

Dangerous commands visibly implement noninteractive IaC teardown and follow the source ask/critical default. None establishes explicit production, approval, backups, ownership or recovery guarantees; assigning deny solely because deletion occurs would violate the task. Example account identifiers do not establish real customer identity or production scope.

AWS commands are non-confirming destructive API invocations with complete required arguments under ordinary default CLI behavior; optional user configuration such as auto-prompt can alter interaction but is not evidence of an approval step in these examples. Asynchronous deletion, IAM failures, protection, retention and partial operation failures must not be described as proof of safety or guaranteed completed destruction.
